ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9028.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9028.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The same service can be maintained at lower cost by changing an existing bundle, which is the substitution mechanism. A travel example alone does not measure the full index’s bias or imply that overall prices fell.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9028.key: A fixed bundle overstates the cost of that service; the evidence does not quantify bias for the whole CPI

PM2B2-BIAS-L-001.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
PM2B2-BIAS-L-001.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: A cheaper bundle can reflect reduced consumption or quality rather than cost-saving substitution at the same living standard. The comparison must hold the relevant standard of living constant before interpreting the gap as bias.
PM2B2-BIAS-L-001.key: The redesigned bundle preserves the relevant living standard, with comparable quality and coverage

PM2B2-DEF-H-002.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
PM2B2-DEF-H-002.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The deflator compares current-price and base-price values of current quantities. Changing the output mix toward larger current-to-base price relatives can raise the ratio even with no new individual price changes. High dollar prices alone do not establish that result.
PM2B2-DEF-H-002.key: Current quantities put more weight on goods with larger price increases since the base year

ECON-NL-ELITE-331.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-ELITE-331.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The household payment needs a consumer-price measure, which includes imported consumer energy. Deflating GDP requires prices of domestic production, including investment goods. Their differing coverage permits divergent movements.
ECON-NL-ELITE-331.key: Use CPI for the allowance and the GDP deflator for GDP; the indexes can move differently

ECON-NL-ELITE-344.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-ELITE-344.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Capital scarcity can create high-return opportunities, but skilled workers and usable infrastructure help realize them. Catch-up is conditional; equal starting capital alone does not establish equal productivity growth.
ECON-NL-ELITE-344.key: The complementary inputs differ, so equal capital scarcity does not imply equal realized gains

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9054.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9054.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The second stage changes human capital while holding physical inputs fixed. Its effect can reflect complementarity between skills and machinery. A weak result before training does not identify a zero contribution from capital.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9054.key: Training helped realize the value of complementary capital; the first stage did not show that machines were useless

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9056.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9056.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: A new production method is technological knowledge; skills acquired by workers are human capital. Equal measured gains do not identify a common mechanism or prove the two interventions would have equal effects elsewhere.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9056.key: A changed technological knowledge and B human capital; equal output gains do not make the mechanisms identical

ECON-NL-LEGENDARYBOSS-9120.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARYBOSS-9120.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Diminishing marginal returns concerns additional capital with other determinants held fixed. The first two gains fit that pattern. A technology improvement changes the production relationship, so the larger third gain is not a comparable capital-only experiment.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARYBOSS-9120.key: No; the first two gains compare capital with other inputs fixed, while technology changed in the third

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9060.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9060.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The evidence identifies insecure returns as a barrier between available funds and investment. Predictable enforcement can complement financing. The survey does not establish an optimal subsidy or prove capital has no productive value.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9060.key: Address enforcement risk alongside finance; more saving alone may not make productive investment attractive

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9062.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9062.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The constrained margin is adopting better methods. Technology, skills and equipment can complement one another; repeating one input policy while blocking another can limit the gain. This is a conditional recommendation from the stated evidence.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9062.key: Permit useful method adoption while maintaining skills and investment; training alone may not release the constraint

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9063.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9063.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The instruments address institutions, human capital and technological knowledge. These are plausible growth channels, but observed short-run output alone neither guarantees eventual success nor disproves the channels. Implementation and technology diffusion must be evaluated.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9063.key: The package targets productivity determinants; implementation, diffusion and time still matter for realized growth

ECON-NL-ELITE-359.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-ELITE-359.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Additional capital can still raise output, but its marginal contribution may diminish with other inputs fixed. Skills and technological progress complement capital and support productivity growth beyond a single level increase.
ECON-NL-ELITE-359.key: Maintain useful investment while improving skills, research and adoption of better methods

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9084.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9084.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Unemployment divides job seekers by the labor force. Lower participation can lower employment per adult even at the same rate, while involuntary part-time workers remain employed. Additional participation and hours evidence is needed for the broader assessment.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9084.key: Compare employment per adult and desired versus actual hours; the headline rate omits both differences

ECON-NL-FINALBOSS-4006.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-FINALBOSS-4006.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The worker moves from outside the labor force to employed. Both employment and the labor force rise, while wanting more hours does not change the official employed classification. The hours shortfall remains relevant to labor-market well-being.
ECON-NL-FINALBOSS-4006.key: Employment and the labor force rise; involuntary part-time work can remain

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9074.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9074.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Normal matching among suitable jobs is frictional; a persistent credential mismatch is structural. A paid part-time job makes the third group employed under the official measure, even though underemployment may remain.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9074.key: The first group is frictionally unemployed, the second structurally unemployed, and the third employed

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9080.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9080.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The mismatch between expanding occupations and worker credentials points to a structural barrier. Placements after relevant training, with demand broadly unchanged, strengthen that mechanism rather than a claim based only on weak spending or ordinary search.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9080.key: Credential training is followed by placements into the unfilled occupations while overall spending changes little

PM2B4-UTYPE-L-002.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
PM2B4-UTYPE-L-002.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: The first group faces search frictions among suitable jobs. The second faces a durable mismatch that information alone may not remove. Diagnosis should guide the intervention without assuming guaranteed placement.
PM2B4-UTYPE-L-002.key: It can shorten matching for the first group; the second may also need retraining or mobility support

ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9077.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9077.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Income support can reduce search urgency while better matching shortens search. Their combined result does not isolate either effect; a credible separate comparison would be needed. The duration result also does not measure the value of income protection.
ECON-NL-LEGENDARY-9077.key: The combined outcome improved duration; it does not show that the benefit extension by itself shortened search

ECON-NL-ELITE-379.method: Each alternative reviewed against the stated mechanism and assumptions. Incidental numbers do not determine a numerical answer.
ECON-NL-ELITE-379.uniqueCorrectnessRationale: Both totals equal 5%, but the components differ. A common aggregate benchmark does not establish identical barriers or identical policy priorities. Relevant retraining and matching interventions target different components.
ECON-NL-ELITE-379.key: The first has more mismatch to address; the second has more scope for faster matching, holding effectiveness comparable
